note: A value the calculation consumes. This file is the answer to 'how do I select the right parameters for this case': every slot states who is allowed to supply it (`supplied_via`), which authority governs it, which operator reads it, what happens when it is absent, and which uncertainty or guardrail fires. A slot never carries a formula: formulas live in knowledge/operators.json and are selected through branches. The questionnaire can only fill slots, so an intake form can never invent a calculation rule.

slots.name: Date of the event
slots.select: Take the occurrence date from the authority report where one exists, otherwise from the declaration; record which. It fixes the Iranian claim year and therefore the depreciation year index.
slots.validation: not after the declaration date; inside the policy period

slots.name: Date the insured became aware of the loss
slots.select: The five-working-day notice clock runs from awareness, not from occurrence. Ask for both and never derive awareness from occurrence.

slots.name: Date the loss was declared to the insurer
slots.select: Insurer practice sometimes counts the sixty-day theft clock from declaration while the regulation counts it from the theft. Record the declaration date anyway, because the settlement clocks in the payment provision run from complete documents.

slots.name: Whether notice complied with the duty
slots.select: LATE only raises a review gate; it does not zero the claim, because the regulation excuses non-compliance caused by unavoidable events.

slots.name: Iranian year used for depreciation and annual parameters
slots.select: Use the Iranian year of the event, not the settlement year. Review preserves a missing event year as unknown and emits no snapshot year. Direct calc still has a legacy year fallback; P0-01 and P1-02 must close that bypass.

slots.name: Insured peril that caused the loss
slots.select: Choose from the closed peril list of the regulation (collision-type events, fire/lightning/explosion, theft or theft attempt, damage during rescue or transport, battery and tyre loss) or from an endorsement peril. Never infer a peril from the damaged part.

slots.name: Whether the peril is the cause of this damage
slots.select: Causation is a predicate, never a multiplier. If the causal link is asserted but not evidenced, the case routes to review; it does not attract a coefficient.

slots.name: Which theft situation applies
slots.select: Whole vehicle, attempted theft that damaged the vehicle, or theft of parts and accessories. The three take different routes: total settlement, partial damage, or the parts-theft endorsement.

slots.name: Days since the vehicle went missing
slots.select: Fifty-nine days is pending, sixty is total loss. Record which date the count starts from, because the regulation, the payment provision and insurer practice anchor on different dates.

slots.name: Registration transferred to the insurer
slots.select: Total theft settlement requires the transfer first. Where title passes, salvage must not also be subtracted.

slots.name: Transactional value of the vehicle on the accident date
slots.select: One figure, three jobs: the 75% total-loss denominator, the underinsurance denominator, and the total-loss settlement base. Never substitute the insured sum or a purchase price.

slots.name: Insured sum stated in the policy
slots.select: Read it off the declarations page for the policy year of the event. Supplying only one of insured sum and market value is an error, not a ratio of one.
slots.validation: if both supplied and insured > market, cap the settlement base at market

slots.name: Underinsurance ratio (قاعده نسبی)
slots.select: min(1, insured_sum / market_value). It is a ratio, not a deduction, and it is capped at one: over-insurance cannot increase a payment. Where it is below one in a partial loss, the pipeline position is unresolved and the result must be a scenario set.

slots.name: Production (model) year of the vehicle
slots.select: The depreciation year index is claim_year - production_year + 1, so this single field decides whether depreciation is 0%, mid-schedule or at the 25% ceiling. Take it from the registration or the policy schedule, not from the odometer or the owner's memory.

slots.name: Assessed gross damage before deductions
slots.select: Prefer an itemised parts-plus-labour assessment; use an aggregate only when the assessment cannot be itemised, and label the result ITEMISED_PARTS_USED vs aggregate accordingly.

slots.name: Fair repair labour
slots.select: Labour is not depreciated: the depreciation operator applies to replaced parts, so a labour figure inside an undifferentiated 'total repair cost' overstates the deduction.

slots.name: Category of each damaged component
slots.select: Closed vocabulary: GLASS, LAMP_GLASS, BATTERY, TIRE, OTHER_REPLACEMENT_PART, REPAIR_ONLY. The category decides exemption from depreciation, the 50%-of-new cap, and whether the item enters the total-loss numerator at all.
slots.validation: unknown spellings are rejected rather than defaulted

slots.name: New price of a capped component
slots.select: Required for BATTERY and TIRE because the covered loss is capped at 50% of the new price. Whether that cap and the age schedule stack is unresolved, so for an older vehicle the engine stops rather than stacking them.

slots.name: Depreciation as assessed, versus as computed
slots.select: If the assessor states depreciation explicitly, carry it and record depreciation_source=EXPLICIT. Otherwise let the operator compute it per part and record COMPUTED_PER_PART. Never mix the two in one claim.

slots.name: Actual rescue, mitigation and transport cost
slots.select: Claimed cost is not payable cost: it is added after the 20% ceiling is applied, and the same figure is part of the total-loss numerator.

slots.name: Denominator of the 20% rescue ceiling
slots.select: The regulation says 20% of total damage without defining the denominator. Record the selected base. If no base is supplied, continue only when every candidate base produces the same capped rescue amount; otherwise surface U05.

slots.name: Repair and replacement cost used for the total-loss test
slots.select: The numerator is repair and replacement cost WITH rescue and transport included, against 75% of the value on the accident date. A declared total loss without this evidence must not settle.

slots.name: Probable salvage value
slots.select: Salvage is deducted from the settlement base before the total-loss franchise is computed, per the Central Insurance clarification. It is not damage, so it is not depreciated or franchised on its own.

slots.name: Who keeps the wreck
slots.select: INSURED_RETAINS means subtract salvage; INSURER_TAKES_TITLE means transfer the wreck and do not subtract its value. UNRESOLVED must block rather than pick.

slots.name: Franchise terms: mode, rate, minimum, base, claim sequence, coverage rule, source version
slots.select: There is no universal rate. A percentage must name its calculation base and its source instrument and version; an unsourced percentage is refused, and a missing franchise blocks on U02 instead of becoming zero.

slots.name: Endorsements actually held, with their printed terms
slots.select: Two different facts: that an endorsement exists, and what its schedule says. Only the second one lets a branch return a number.

slots.name: Whether the glass damage arose from a covered collision-type peril
slots.select: If glass broke together with other damage from an insured peril, the claim is ordinary partial damage, not standalone glass. The standalone route is only for causes outside the insurer's basic perils.

slots.name: The glass-only cover's own valuation condition
slots.select: At least one insurer's printed glass endorsement conditions payment on the vehicle being insured at market value, which would remove the standalone route entirely for an under-insured vehicle. It is a policy term, not a regulation rule: read the wording, do not generalise it.

slots.name: Where the underinsurance ratio runs relative to the franchise in a partial loss
slots.select: UNRESOLVED is the honest default: the regulation mandates both operators and fixes no sequence. Only an insurer worksheet or an official clarification may set it, and the setting must be recorded with its source.

slots.name: How the 50% cap and the age schedule combine
slots.select: Only live when a battery or tyre is damaged on a vehicle whose depreciation year index has reached five.

slots.name: Cash indemnity, repair in kind, or replacement vehicle
slots.select: The mode changes the delivery, not the arithmetic: the regulation states that in any case franchise and depreciation remain the insured's responsibility. Do not let a repair-in-kind settlement drop either operator.

slots.name: Other policies and prior compensation for the same loss
slots.select: Record both whether another policy covers the same risk and every amount already received for this loss. Without fraudulent intent the paying insurer settles and then pursues contribution; the insured may never recover twice.

slots.name: Whether the insured impaired the insurer's recourse
slots.select: A release or settlement with the responsible party is a review gate that can deny or recover payment; it is not a deduction the calculator may apply.

slots.name: Unnotified intensification of risk
slots.select: Where it applies, the regulation reduces payment by the ratio of the premium charged to the premium appropriate to the intensified risk. That premium-ratio mechanism is a different operator from underinsurance and is NOT implemented in the calculation engine: the case must be escalated, never approximated by the ratio.

slots.name: Licence class, validity and appropriateness for the vehicle
slots.select: Three different states, three different outcomes: valid, expired (which the regulation says is not the same as void), and void or inappropriate for the class (non-compensable). A single yes/no field cannot carry that distinction.

slots.name: Intoxication causally established by a competent authority
slots.select: Both parts are required: an authority report and a causal link to the loss. Absent either, the exclusion does not fire.
